name: Playlist
description: Arkady has a playlist that initially consists of $$$n$$$ songs, numerated from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ in the order they appear in the playlist. Arkady starts listening to the songs in the playlist one by one, starting from song $$$1$$$. The playlist is cycled, i. e. after listening to the last song, Arkady will continue listening from the beginning. Each song has a genre $$$a_i$$$, which is a positive integer. Let Arkady finish listening to a song with genre $$$y$$$, and the genre of the next-to-last listened song be $$$x$$$. If $$$\operatorname{gcd}(x, y) = 1$$$, he deletes the last listened song (with genre $$$y$$$) from the playlist. After that he continues listening normally, skipping the deleted songs, and forgetting about songs he listened to before. In other words, after he deletes a song, he can't delete the next song immediately. Here $$$\operatorname{gcd}(x, y)$$$ denotes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$. For example, if the initial songs' genres were $$$[5, 9, 2, 10, 15]$$$, then the playlist is converted as follows: [ 5 , 9, 2, 10, 15] $$$\to$$$ [ 5 , 9 , 2, 10, 15] $$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10, 15] (because $$$\operatorname{gcd}(5, 9) = 1$$$) $$$\to$$$ [5, 2 , 10, 15] $$$\to$$$ [5, 2 , 10 , 15] $$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10 , 15 ] $$$\to$$$ [ 5 , 2, 10, 15 ] $$$\to$$$ [ 5 , 2 , 10, 15] $$$\to$$$ [5, 10, 15] (because $$$\operatorname{gcd}(5, 2) = 1$$$) $$$\to$$$ [5, 10 , 15] $$$\to$$$ [5, 10 , 15 ] $$$\to$$$ ... The bold numbers represent the two last played songs. Note that after a song is deleted, Arkady forgets that he listened to that and the previous songs. Given the initial playlist, please determine which songs are eventually deleted and the order these songs are deleted.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10\,000$$$). Description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the number of songs. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the genres of the songs. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print a single line. First, print a single integer $$$k$$$ — the number of deleted songs. After that print $$$k$$$ distinct integers: deleted songs in the order of their deletion.
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1482D — Playlist [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
